findings.reason: a worker implementing §2 as written cannot satisfy done-when case 4 inside its scope; it either fails its own gate or silently widens its write paths, so §2 must either add the row-writing path to its write paths or drop the record key from the done-when.
findings.text: §2's fourth done-when case requires "the promotion record's `red_base_bare_matches` names the bare name and both ids", but the ledger row stores `_normalized_gate_check(gate_check)` (`reckon/ledger.py:472`), which rebuilds the check from only `command`, `exit_status`, `log_path` and `log_digest`, so any key the admission adds in `promotion_evidence.py` is discarded before the row is written — and the only places the key can survive are `reckon/ledger.py` or the row augmentation in `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, neither of which is in §2's declared write paths (`reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`, `reckon/crew/review.py`, the new test)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` (`_zero_added_against_a_red_base`, line 1174) and `reckon/crew/review.py` (`canonical_node_id`, line 1938) both exist and match what §2 says they do.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2 declares four measurable cases plus a negative control (exact id comparison, first case fails), a no-added-failure check against the base revision, and a ruff delta; the multi-match case the previous review asked for is now present and tested.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the node writes its gate to the run's own log paths; no scratchpad or node-local temporary path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `red_base_bare_matches` names the mechanism, not a plan label, ticket or version.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated root cause and the matching mechanism hold, but the mechanism cannot write the record key §2's fourth done-when case asserts, because the row normaliser drops it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the matching rule, the refusal that names uncovered ids, and the record key are one deliverable: the red-base admission's handling of ids the base does not cover.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` names only `s4 -> s2`, and §2 depends on no other section; the three sections write disjoint files, matching the followup's claim.
